## Overview

The high-denominator half of the dispersion pair (#605). This is [LRP97](../lrp-rli-mech-097) with **one** thing changed: the Beta-Binomial concentration is put on the dispersion scale, $1/\sqrt{\kappa} \sim \text{HalfNormal}(0.25)$, instead of the family's shared $\kappa \sim \text{HalfNormal}(50)$. [LRP304](../lrp-rli-mech-304) is the word-reading channel and carries the fuller account of why the shared prior is not weak.

**Why this outcome.** Receptive vocabulary has the family's largest denominator (170 items), where the registered prior bites hardest. At its own median ($\kappa \approx 33.7$) it implies a **5.87×** variance inflation over Binomial, and coming within 10 % of Binomial would need $\kappa > 1689$ — a region $\text{HalfNormal}(50)$ gives effectively zero mass. Four registered mechanism fits sit at this denominator; if the prior is binding anywhere in the family, it is here.

## How to read it

Exactly as LRP304: does the family's declared items-scale headline contrast move when the model is *allowed* to conclude there is no extra-Binomial dispersion, and did the data move $\kappa$ at all? The dispersion table below publishes the posterior concentration against its prior and the implied variance-inflation factor.

## Adjustment set

$\{G, A, HS, IS, SP\}$ plus baseline $R_\text{pre}$ — identical to LRP97, the matched Tier-1 conditioning set. GA is unblockable; $\beta_\text{mech}$ is an **adjusted association**.
